title: Effects of Irrigation Protocols Relevant to Regenerative Endodontics on Root Dentin Gelatinolytic Activity and Matrix Metalloproteinase-2 And -9 Immunolabeling.
source: PubMed · Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
byline: Jacob G, Villamayor K, Assis H, et al.
html:
Objective: Irrigation in regenerative endodontics must balance disinfection with preservation of the dentin matrix, whose matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) may be exposed or degraded by irrigants. This study evaluated the effects of irrigation protocols on gelatinolytic activity and MMP-2 and MMP-9 immunolabeling in root dentin.

Materials and methods: In this randomized, examiner-blinded ex vivo study, thirty single-rooted teeth with standardized open apices were allocated to five protocols (n = 6): saline (G1); 1.5% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl; G2); saline followed by 17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA; G3); 1.5% NaOCl, saline, and EDTA (G4); or 2.5% NaOCl, saline, and EDTA (G5). Cervical, middle, and apical slices were analyzed by in situ zymography and immunofluorescence. Data were analyzed by two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey-adjusted comparisons (α = 0.05).

Results: Irrigation protocol and root third affected all outcomes (p < 0.0001). Protocol-by-third interactions occurred for MMP-2 and MMP-9 (both p < 0.0001), but not gelatinolytic activity (p = 0.1619). Across root thirds, G3 showed the highest gelatinolytic activity (27.73 ± 1.74 pixels/µm²) and G2 the lowest (11.65 ± 0.62 pixels/µm²). Gelatinolytic activity was lower apically (16.02 ± 5.76 pixels/µm²) than cervically (19.79 ± 6.42) and in the middle third (18.48 ± 5.98). In the apical third, MMP-2 ranged from 27.88 ± 1.04 in G3 to 11.70 ± 0.94 pixels/µm² in G2, and MMP-9 from 24.63 ± 1.62 to 7.96 ± 1.04 pixels/µm², respectively.

Conclusion: Irrigation protocols distinctly modulated the proteolytic profile of root dentin along the root. Whether these changes influence regenerative outcomes remains to be determined.
